coordinates: Blender: Z up, creature faces -Y, +X = creature left. Normalized so the reference dimension = 1.0

rigs.description: Slimes and oozes: a gel dome with jiggle lobes. Moves by hopping; squash & stretch is the whole performance.
Tiny two-legged critters with no real arms: walking mushrooms, mandrakes, sprouts. Waddle gait, huge head/cap.
Goblins, kobolds, imps: 0.8–1.3 m. Oversized head and hands, short bowed legs, hunched spine. Humanoid-retargetable (Mixamo works with tweaks).
Human-scale bipeds 1.5–2.2 m. Standard Humanoid avatar so Mixamo and asset-store packs retarget directly.
Hulking bipeds 2.5–5 m: wide shoulders, long arms (can knuckle-walk), heavy footfalls. Humanoid avatar with an extra belly jiggle bone.
Giants 6–20 m. Same skeleton as large_biped plus climbable surfaces and weak-point sockets. Player can climb onto them (Shadow of the Colossus style grab points).
Constructs: rigid segments (no skin deformation, every mesh piece parented to one bone), a glowing core. Joints may float with visible gaps.
Small quadrupeds 0.3–0.8 m long. Hind-dominant: hopping or bounding gaits, ears and tail are their acting.
Medium quadrupeds 1–2.5 m long. Full gait set (walk/trot/gallop), circling and pack flanking.
Heavy quadrupeds 2.5–8 m. Can rear up on hind legs (bears). Charges are its signature.
Four legs + a separate pair of wings (6 limbs): dragons, griffons, manticores. Long neck and tail. Flies in boss fights; never a mount (Canon).
Six-legged insects. Tripod gait (3 legs down at once), procedural leg IK on uneven ground. Mandibles and antennae act.
Eight legs, cephalothorax + abdomen. Wave gait, wall and ceiling walking, web anchors. Menace-heavy: stillness then sudden speed.
Limbless long bodies: snakes, giant worms, eels, sea serpents. Spline-driven spine (16 bones) with a follow-the-head path solver.
Humanoid torso on a serpent tail: nagas, lamias. Upper body uses humanoid arm/head bones; lower uses the serpent spine.
Humanoid torso on a four-legged body: centaurs. Lower body uses quad gaits; upper body aims weapons independently.
Feathered fliers. Hops on the ground, flaps/glides in air, dive attacks. Feather chains are spring bones.
Bat-winged fliers: membrane wings on finger bones. Erratic flight, ceiling hang, swoops.
Two legs + wings that double as front limbs (walks on wing-knuckles). Lighter and faster than dragons.
Legless floating beings. No gravity, motion from noise curves; a trailing tail chain made of VFX. Phases through thin walls (Menace 4+).
Rooted plants that attack in place: man-eating flowers, vine traps, ambush trees. Can uproot to relocate slowly.
Fish-like swimmers. Body-wave swimming (carangiform), leap attacks out of water, flops on land.
Mantle + 8 tentacles (6 bones each). Tentacles are FABRIK chains that reach for targets; ink and grab attacks.
A cloud of tiny units acting as one monster. One controller bone; units are GPU-instanced (VFX Graph or particle system) with boid rules. HP shown as density.

unitRig.note: Each unit: 1–3 bones (body + 2 wings) animated by vertex shader flutter, not bones

rigs.description: Menace-5 bodies that break symmetry: a core with 6 procedural limbs that can reattach, a mimic socket that copies other rigs' silhouettes. Audio-first reveals.
